what_this_means_for_you.in_short: PROPOSAL: Creates a new municipality (Ligawasan). If you live in the covered barangays, your community gets its own municipal government - a mayor, sanggunian, municipal hall, and its own share of national and regional funds - instead of being administered from a distant town center. (This describes what the bill would do if enacted.)
in_practice: Your own municipal share of the National Tax Allotment and Bangsamoro funds, spent locally
Closer civil registry, business permits, social services, and health station
Local elections for your own mayor, vice mayor, and councilors once the LGU is organized
Barangay boundaries stay; what changes is which town hall serves you

for_specific_groups.Residents: Government services move closer; local projects are decided by officials you elect
for_specific_groups.Business owners: Permits and local taxes are handled by the new municipality - rates are set by its own sanggunian
for_specific_groups.Job seekers: A new LGU means new municipal government positions
for_specific_groups.SGA residents: For the eight 2023 municipalities: these convert the Special Geographic Area's 63 barangays (which voted to join BARMM) into full local governments

watch_out_for: Nothing changes yet: a bill has no legal effect until Parliament approves it and it is enacted as a Bangsamoro Autonomy Act. Many bills are revised or merged along the way.
A new municipality begins corporate existence only after its officials are elected/qualified and offices organized - there is a transition period
Boundary and asset-sharing details with the mother municipality can take time to settle
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Not yet - only if and when enacted
what_you_can_do: This is the stage where public input matters most: submit a position paper via the Parliament's 'Call for Position Papers' page
Attend or watch the committee hearings (schedules are on the Parliament site; many are livestreamed)
Contact a Member of Parliament - the 'Contact an MP' page lists them - to support, oppose, or suggest changes

key_terms_explained.First Reading: The bill's title is read in plenary and it is referred to a committee - the earliest formal stage.
key_terms_explained.Committee stage: A committee studies the bill, holds hearings, and can rewrite it before plenary debate.
key_terms_explained.BAA: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act - a regional law passed by the Bangsamoro Parliament, applying inside BARMM alongside national laws.

benefits.headline: Your own local government - services, budget, and representation for Ligawasan.

direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic; monitor via the municipal budget and sanggunian sessions

direct_benefits.benefit: Your own elected mayor, vice mayor, and councilors answerable to you
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Vote in the first municipal elections

direct_benefits.benefit: New municipal government jobs and local contracts

indirect_benefits: Recognition: for SGA towns, the plebiscite promise made real
limitations: Now REAL, not prospective: enacted as BAA 48 - see baa/BAA-48.json for claimable benefits.
